carnage.name: Codylt93
carnage.commentary: The wheels came off at 16: seven shots on a par 3 is the kind of mess that turns a card into a crime scene. That was the ugliest number on the sheet, but the damage was bigger than one hole: 3 doubles or worse, 2 three-putts, and a short game that got absolutely smoked.

carnage.name: Leedaddy23
carnage.commentary: Six on a par 3 at 6. That’s the whole problem right there: one hole turned into a little hostage situation and the rest of the round spent trying to unfuck the math. You can survive a few misses; you can’t donate a triple-looking number to a par 3 and pretend it’s tidy.

carnage.name: Wardus
carnage.commentary: Opening-hole four on a par 3 is a rude hello. It wasn’t a collapse, just the kind of first-hole bogey energy that says the round has a pulse before the golf starts behaving.

carnage.name: RosaryJoe
carnage.commentary: The first-hole four set the tone: not a disaster, but immediately behind the eight ball. And when you follow that with more of the same, the card starts looking like it got stuck in traffic instead of making birdies.

carnage.name: frthomas2
carnage.commentary: First-hole three: the least dramatic crime in the batch. No shots listed, no circus, just a par 3 that behaved like a par 3 and didn’t hand out free damage.

carnage.name: TakeitlowGolf29
carnage.commentary: Same deal on 1: three on a par 3, clean and boring in the best possible way. No shot sequence drama, no wasted strokes, just the kind of start that doesn’t light the card on fire.

players.name: frthomas2
players.tagline: The card was cleaner than your buddy’s excuses.
players.body: Tied for 7th in net and 5th in gross, and this was the kind of round where the ball-striking did the yelling. The profile is loud: +3.99 approach, +4.30 short game, +1.21 putting, and a ridiculous +9.5 total with 16 greens in regulation, 8 birdies, and zero bogeys. He didn’t need hero stuff off the tee; he just kept stacking pars and birdies while the card stayed clean. The worst-hole line is basically a shrug: the opening par 3 was just a par, which is exactly how you avoid giving strokes back in a field like this. With no prior completed starts to compare against, we’re not calling a trend yet, but the current round was straight-up business.

players.name: TakeitlowGolf29
players.tagline: Quiet round, loud short game, zero respect for the scoring average.
players.body: Net 8th, gross 6th, and the weirdest part is how steady the thing stayed while still leaking a little in the long game. He posted +2.71 approach, +4.96 short game, and +1.83 putting for a +9.5 total, with 11 GIR, 8 birdies, 3/3 sand saves, and only 21 putts. That’s a pretty clean scoring profile even if the approach numbers weren’t as sharp as the others near the top. The worst hole was just an opening par on a par 3, so there was no blow-up lurking in the shadows; this was more “win every little fight” than “steamroll the course.” With zero prior profile-eligible starts, the only real read is on the round itself, and it was quietly solid.

players.name: Wardus
players.tagline: Putted like he found a cheat code and still left a couple bogeys on the table.
players.body: Net 9th, gross 7th, and this one was all about the flatstick papering over some less-than-clean work elsewhere. The +4.46 putting was the loudest number in the round, backed by +3.03 short game and a modest +1.01 approach, good for an +8.5 total. He made 9 birdies, hit 12 greens, and kept the putts to 21, which is why the card stayed playable even with 2 bogeys hanging around. The opening-hole four on a par 3 was the first dent, and he matched that same number again on 11, so the round had just enough bleed in it to keep him off the podium conversation. With no prior starts in the file, this is just a strong one-round snapshot: good enough to score, not sharp enough to separate.

players.name: Leedaddy23
players.tagline: The scorecard was held together with duct tape and a prayer.
players.body: Net 10th and gross 43rd is the kind of split that tells you the raw golf was a mess even if the net card stayed semi-respectable. He finished with a -4.5 total, powered by a rough -2.09 approach, -1.28 short game, and -1.14 putting, plus just 7 greens in regulation, 5 bogeys, and 27 putts. The one thing the card had going for it was avoiding total meltdown: no doubles, and he did make a couple birdies, but the underlying numbers were ugly. The worst hole was the par 3 at 6, where he needed six shots gross and five net, and that’s the kind of hole that absolutely wrecks a scorecard’s self-esteem. With no prior completed starts, this is all current-round evidence, and the evidence says the scoring was hanging on while the actual golf was getting punched in the mouth.

players.name: Codylt93
players.tagline: A back-nine faceplant wearing a golf shirt.
players.body: Net 11th, gross 46th, and the raw-card damage was brutal enough to swamp anything decent hiding underneath. The total came out to -10.5, driven by a savage -3.84 approach and -7.10 short game, which is how you end up with 3 double bogeys or worse, 2 three-putts, and 32 putts. He did make 2 birdies and actually putted a little better than the rest of the bag suggested, but that’s not enough when the rest of the round is actively setting itself on fire. The worst hole was 16, where a par 3 ballooned to seven shots gross and net, and that’s the headline because nothing else on the card was trying hard enough to compete with it. With no prior starts to compare against, the only fair read is that this was a wreck from tee-to-green and a full-on short-game implosion.

players.name: RosaryJoe
players.tagline: A pile of almosts, which is golf’s favorite way to waste your afternoon.
players.body: Net 12th and gross 25th, so the card lived in the middle of the pack without ever really threatening the pointy end. The underlying numbers were mixed: +2.13 short game and a +1.75 tee-to-green helped keep things afloat, but -0.38 approach and -0.25 putting kept the round from turning into anything sharper than even-par net. He had 5 birdies, 5 bogeys, 23 putts, and a single three-putt, which is basically the definition of “fine, but not dangerous.” The worst hole was the opener, a par 3 that became a four, and there were enough similar blips early to keep the round from building momentum. With no prior profile-eligible starts, there’s no trend to call; this was just a mixed bag that never picked a lane.
